chapters.summary: Jesus begins his ministry, calls his first disciples, and reveals his authority by healing the sick and casting out unclean spirits.
keyPoints: John the Baptist prepares the way; Jesus is baptized and then tempted in the wilderness.
Jesus proclaims the gospel of God in Galilee and calls his first disciples.
Jesus casts out demons and heals the sick, revealing the authority of the kingdom of God.
chapters.application: Today, let us respond to Jesus' call, trust in his authority, and proclaim in our daily lives the good news of repentance and faith in the gospel.

chapters.summary: In Capernaum, Jesus heals a paralyzed man, calls Levi, and debates the Pharisees over the true meaning of the Sabbath, revealing that he is Lord both to forgive sins and over the Sabbath.
keyPoints: Four friends tear open a roof to lower a paralyzed man down to Jesus; seeing their faith, Jesus declares his sins forgiven and heals him, showing that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins.
Jesus calls the tax collector Levi and eats with sinners, showing that he did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.

Using the parables of the bridegroom and the old wineskins, Jesus explains that new life cannot be confined by old rules; he is Lord of the Sabbath, and his disciples plucking heads of grain on the Sabbath breaks no law.
chapters.application: Let us come to Jesus in faith, for he can forgive our sins and heal us; and let us hold on to a new heart, unbound by tradition and rules, finding true rest in Christ.

chapters.summary: Jesus heals on the Sabbath, appoints the twelve disciples, and speaks about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit and about who truly belongs to the family of those who do God's will.
keyPoints: Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath, revealing compassion and the true meaning of the law.
Jesus appoints twelve disciples, that they might be with him and be sent out to preach.
The scribes accuse Jesus of casting out demons by the prince of demons, and Jesus warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven.
chapters.application: Let us examine whether we allow rules to override compassion, whether we are willing to be with Jesus and do God's will, and let us guard our words so as never to blaspheme the Holy Spirit.

chapters.summary: Jesus uses the parable of the sower to teach the truth of the kingdom, and instructs his disciples to listen carefully, for how we receive the word determines the harvest of our lives.
keyPoints: In the parable of the sower, the seed is the word, and the four types of soil represent the different ways people's hearts respond to it.
Jesus explains the parable, showing that the disciples are blessed to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of God, while those outside cannot.
As Jesus and the disciples crossed the sea, a fierce storm arose; he rebuked the wind and it was still, and the amazed disciples were asked why they were so fearful and had no faith.
themes: Hearing the Word and Bearing Fruit
chapters.application: As we read God's word each day, let us ask the Lord to make our hearts good soil, so that his word may take root and bear fruit; and in life's storms, let us trust his word all the more, and find peace and calm.

chapters.summary: Jesus casts out an unclean spirit in the region of the Gadarenes, heals a woman with a flow of blood, and raises Jairus' daughter from the dead, revealing his power over unclean spirits, sickness, and death.
keyPoints: Jesus casts a legion of demons out of a man in the region of the Gadarenes; the demons enter a herd of pigs, which rush down the bank into the sea and drown.
A woman who had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years touches Jesus' garment in faith and is instantly healed, and Jesus commends her faith.
Jesus raises the daughter of Jairus, a synagogue ruler, from the dead, showing that he has authority over life itself.
chapters.application: Whatever difficulty we face, let us follow the example of the woman's faith, boldly drawing near to Jesus, for he will surely have compassion on us and heal us.

chapters.summary: Jesus is rejected in his hometown, sends out his disciples to preach, learns of John the Baptist's martyrdom, and reveals his authority and compassion by feeding five thousand with five loaves and two fish and walking on the sea.
keyPoints: Jesus is despised in Nazareth, and because of his hometown's unbelief, he can do few mighty works there.
Jesus sends out the twelve disciples two by two to preach, and they cast out demons and heal the sick.
Jesus feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, then walks on the water, leaving the disciples astonished.
chapters.application: When our faith grows weak, let us remember that Jesus' power is greater than any circumstance; he has compassion on us as sheep without a shepherd, so let us trust him and boldly proclaim his name.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches that true cleanness is a matter of the heart, and reveals his power by healing a Gentile.
keyPoints: The Pharisees, holding fast to the tradition of the elders, criticize the disciples for eating without washing their hands.
Jesus points out their hypocrisy - honoring God with their lips while their hearts are far from him.
Defilement comes from within the heart, but those who trust in Jesus can receive cleansing and healing.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts, not allowing outward rules to replace a heart that loves God and loves others, and let us receive God's cleansing and grace by faith.

chapters.summary: Jesus feeds four thousand with seven loaves and warns the disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees; he then heals a blind man at Bethsaida, Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, Jesus foretells his suffering and resurrection, and he calls all people to take up their cross and follow him.
keyPoints: Moved with compassion for the crowd, Jesus feeds four thousand people with seven loaves and a few small fish, showing his provision and love.
Jesus warns the disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod - that is, false teaching and unbelief.
Peter confesses that Jesus is the Christ, Jesus foretells for the first time his suffering and resurrection, and he teaches the disciples to deny themselves and follow him.
themes: Denying Self to Follow the Lord
chapters.application: In our daily lives, let us trust in the Lord's provision, stay alert to false teaching, and be willing to take up our own cross, denying ourselves to follow Jesus and living out a love and obedience that lets go of self.

chapters.summary: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain, teaches his disciples about faith and humility, and warns of the seriousness of sin.
keyPoints: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain, revealing his glory, and the disciples witness his majesty.
Jesus heals a boy possessed by an unclean spirit, emphasizing the importance of faith and prayer.
Jesus teaches the disciples to serve with humility, and warns of the seriousness of causing others to stumble.
chapters.application: Let us depend on the Lord in faith, serve with humility, and watch our words and actions carefully, so that we do not cause others to stumble.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches about marriage, children, wealth, and the cost of discipleship, and heals the blind man Bartimaeus.
keyPoints: Jesus reaffirms the sanctity of marriage and speaks against divorce.
Jesus blesses the little children, emphasizing that the kingdom of God belongs to those who are humble like them.
Jesus tells a rich young man to sell all he has and follow him, and teaches the disciples the example of serving others.
chapters.application: In our families and our work, let us learn to treat others with a humble and serving heart, trust God, refuse to be captivated by wealth, and live out a life that follows Jesus.

chapters.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem in glory, cleanses the temple, curses the fig tree, and teaches his disciples about the authority of faith and prayer.
keyPoints: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey as the crowds cry out 'Hosanna,' fulfilling the prophet's words.
Jesus cleanses the temple, driving out those buying and selling, and rebukes them for turning a house of prayer into a den of robbers.
Jesus curses the fig tree, teaching the disciples to have faith and to forgive others.
chapters.application: Let us ask the Lord for a clean heart, that our lives may become a house of prayer, that we may act in faith, and that we may forgive others freely.

chapters.summary: Through parables and debate, Jesus teaches that loving God and loving others is the sum of the law, and points out that a poor widow's offering is the most precious of all.
keyPoints: The parable of the wicked tenants exposes the rebellion of the religious leaders and foretells their judgment.
Jesus answers questions about paying taxes and the resurrection, showing that God's kingdom surpasses worldly concerns.
The Lord commends the poor widow's two small coins, showing that God values the heart behind the gift, not its amount.
chapters.application: Let us love God with all our heart and love our neighbor as ourselves, giving with an honest heart, for what God values is our trust in him and our obedience.

chapters.summary: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple and the signs of the end times, urging his disciples to watch, be ready, and faithfully await the coming of the Son of man.
keyPoints: Jesus foretells that the temple will be torn down, and the disciples ask when this will happen and what the signs will be.
Jesus warns that the end times will bring false christs, wars, earthquakes, and persecution, but that the gospel must first be preached to all nations.
The Son of man will come on the clouds, and believers must watch and pray, work faithfully, and be ready for the Lord's coming.
themes: The Return of the Son of Man
chapters.application: In the face of a changing world, let us hold on to hope rather than fear, living each day watchfully and faithfully as we wait for the Lord's return.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the preparations before Jesus' suffering, the Last Supper, his prayer in the garden of Gethsemane, Judas' betrayal, and Peter's denial of the Lord.
keyPoints: Mary anoints Jesus with costly ointment, foreshadowing his burial, and is commended by the Lord.
At the Last Supper, Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper and foretells that Judas will betray him.
In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prays and submits to the Father's will, then is arrested and put on trial.
chapters.application: When we face difficult decisions, let us follow Jesus' example of prayer in Gethsemane, laying down our own will, submitting to God's will, and trusting his leading.

chapters.summary: Jesus is tried and condemned before Pilate, mocked by the soldiers, and finally crucified and buried.
keyPoints: Jesus is handed over to Pilate, and though no fault can be found in him, he is condemned because of the crowd's envy.
The soldiers mock Jesus, dressing him in a purple robe and a crown of thorns, jeering at him as the King of the Jews.
Jesus breathes his last on the cross, the centurion declares that he is the Son of God, and Joseph of Arimathaea buries him.
chapters.application: When we face injustice or misunderstanding, let us meditate on Jesus' patience and submission, trust that God is sovereign, and face our hardships with gentleness and faith.

chapters.summary: This chapter records Jesus' resurrection, his appearances to the disciples, his giving of the Great Commission, and his ascension.
keyPoints: The women come to the tomb, find the stone rolled away, and an angel announces that Jesus has risen.
The risen Lord appears to Mary Magdalene, to two disciples, and then to the eleven.
Jesus gives the Great Commission, and the disciples go out to preach the gospel, with the Lord working alongside them and confirming their message.
chapters.application: The risen Lord has conquered death. Let us proclaim the gospel in faith, confident that he will be with us always, even to the end of the age.
